Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
Had my health screening here for an insurance renewal and, unfortunately, the waiting time was the longest I have ever experienced. I arrived at 9:30 AM and was still waiting for my medical report to be finalized at 2 PM, spending more than four hours in total for a routine health screening.
I have been to several medical centres for health screenings before, but this was by far the longest waiting time I have encountered. It seems the centre is receiving a high volume of patients for screenings and medical check-ups, so perhaps additional medical staff could help improve efficiency and reduce waiting times.
The queue numbering system was manageable, although the counters made the process somewhat confusing at times and could be better organized.
That said, I would like to commend the staff for remaining professional, courteous, and smiling throughout the day despite the busy environment. Their positive attitude was appreciated and made the experience more pleasant.

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
I recently visited for a basic health check and ultrasound, having booked my appointment a full week in advance for Friday at 10:00 AM. Unfortunately, the experience was deeply frustrating from start to finish.
Despite arriving on time, I was not seen by a doctor until after 3:30 PM — over five hours of waiting for what should have been a routine visit. Pre-booking an appointment should mean your time is respected; sadly, that was not the case here.
After my ultrasound was completed, staff were unable to locate my report for more than an hour. This caused unnecessary stress and further delayed my consultation. Better systems need to be in place to track patient documents efficiently.
I also found the concierge at Level G to be unhelpful and dismissive. When patients are already dealing with long waits, courteous and proactive staff can make a significant difference — unfortunately, that was lacking here.
I understand that busy days happen, but a 5.5-hour wait for a basic check-up at a private facility — with a prior appointment — is simply not acceptable. I sincerely hope management takes this feedback seriously and works to improve the patient experience. As it stands, I cannot recommend this hospital to others who are time-conscious or expect private-standard service.

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
The service was extremely slow from start to finish. We were informed that the medical report would be ready in approximately 3 hours, so my client arranged his schedule and came early in the morning.
Unfortunately, after waiting for most of the day, the report was still not ready. We were then informed that it could take up to 3 working days instead. This was very frustrating, as it was completely different from what we had been told initially.
If the report cannot realistically be completed within 3 hours, please do not set that expectation. Clear and honest communication is much better than making promises that cannot be fulfilled.
On top of that, the WhatsApp customer service was very slow to respond. We had to wait hours for a reply and repeatedly follow up for updates.
Overall, the experience was disappointing due to the slow service, poor communication, and inconsistent information. I hope the clinic reviews its processes and provides more accurate timelines to future patients.

The call centre staff kept changing, so every time I had to explain the situation from the beginning. I finally received the report after 10 days, and only because I went in person. Very poor experience overall — fine for in-house tests, but unreliable for anything outsourced.

Very disappointing experience.
The biggest issue was the clinic’s extremely poor customer service, especially the team handling the WhatsApp enquiries. I sent multiple messages asking for updates, but no one responded for hours. What’s the point of having a customer care WhatsApp if no one is monitoring it? By the time someone finally replied, it was almost the end of the operating day.
My client arrived early in the morning because we were expecting the check-up and blood test process to be completed efficiently. Instead, everything moved at a very slow pace, and there was no proactive update regarding the test results. We had to keep chasing for information ourselves.
There was also inconsistent information provided by the clinic. We were told over the phone that an appointment was required, yet when my client arrived, other patients were being seen as walk-ins. This caused unnecessary confusion and made us question the clinic’s procedures.
In addition, my client complained that the blood draw was quite painful, making the overall experience even more unpleasant.
It also felt as though panel patients were not being given the same level of priority. I understand this may not be the case, but that was the impression we were left with because of the slow process and lack of communication. Regardless of whether a patient is paying privately or attending under an insurance panel, every patient deserves the same standard of care, efficiency, and respect.
For a private clinic, I expected much better service, communication, and professionalism. Patients should not have to wait hours for a WhatsApp response or repeatedly follow up just to get updates. I sincerely hope the management reviews the customer service standards especially the WhatsApp support team and improves the overall efficiency of the clinic.

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
Mixed experience overall.
On the positive side, the environment is clean and tidy, and once attended to, the staff are generally friendly and provide a pleasant experience.
However, the front desk service was very disappointing. There were 6 counters, yet no one was attending to customers. I waited for about 15 minutes without any acknowledgment. Only after I walked up to the counter myself did they ask me to sit down and begin registration.
I also had a concerning experience during a previous corporate check-up. I was informed by the gynecologist that I had a cyst and that the cost could be claimed through insurance. However, the claim was later rejected, and I had to pay RM500 out of pocket. I then consulted a specialist, who confirmed that there was no issue.
This raises concerns about both service consistency and the accuracy of medical advice provided.
Hoping to see improvements moving forward.

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
This was my first time coming here for a medical checkup, and unfortunately, it was a disappointing experience. While most of the staff and doctors were professional and courteous, I had a particularly unpleasant encounter with one chinese female staff member.
She appeared visibly annoyed while performing her duties and responded to my questions with an irritated tone and expression. At one point, she asked me to prepare for a blood test (I was just standing there waiting for her isntructions, while she was talking to her chinese colleague, and I was 100% sure they were badmouthed me) only to later tell me it wasn’t necessary—without any apology for the confusion or wasted time. Her attitude made the whole process feel unnecessarily stressful and unwelcoming.
On the other hand, I would like to commend one of the Muslim female staff members who handled patients with kindness and professionalism. She made a big difference in the overall experience.
I hope the management addresses these attitude issues with certain staff. Just because the clinic is a panel for many companies doesn't mean patients should be treated rudely. A little respect and courtesy go a long way.

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
I had to do my Australian Immigration Medical Checkup here. The whole process took around 2.5-3 hours. Everything is streamlined here.
Print out the application details form and fill it in before arriving to speed everything up. The only official documents I needed was my original passport which they check before every examination.
I came at 11am. Parking was plentiful and reasonably priced. The lady by the front desk was friendly and thorough with the application form and necessary documents.
I went to the first floor, took a number and waited for a few minutes before being called to register. I had to take a urine sample. Then I paid at the counter past the doors.
They checked my eyesight, blood pressure and took a photo of me for reference.
Then I went for a chest x-ray shortly after.
They called my name for the doctor’s examination about an hour or more later(I left for lunch in between, just sign out t the circular desk in the middle of the hall)
The doctor was very friendly and professional.
And that was all that happened.
Good service overall.

Review:
The centre has good potential, and the staff were courteous and tried their best. However, the overall process and flow could be better managed. Having prior appointments should help control the number of clients per time slot, yet waiting times remain long, suggesting some overbooking or coordination issues.
It may help if the centre pre-prints and pre-registers clients a day before, after reconfirming attendance. This way, clients can simply present their ID and collect their test package upon arrival, instead of queuing just to begin the process.
The queue system could also be more consistent, sometimes numbers are shown on screen, other times names are called out. Mixing both methods creates confusion and slows things down.
With a few small improvements in process design and coordination, the centre could offer a much smoother and more pleasant experience overall.

Review: [Australia Working Holiday Visa 462] Sharing my experience on getting my health assessment done here. I made an appointment via LifeCare app for Saturday morning 7:45am. Parked at the hotel beside and almost got lost. So you need to take the lift to level G and then head outside. Turn left and walk for 2 mins until you see LifeCare. Head in and turn left, the concierge will be there. They will give you a form to fill so just make sure to bring your passport, vaccine certificate and e-medical referral letter. Then head to level 4 and register. Paid RM325 and was done within an hour. They took my blood test, chest X-Ray scan, height and weight measurement, blood pressure and eye check. A simple check-up will also be conducted by a doctor. Overall just try to come early and avoid the crowd. When I left at 9am, there was a huge crowd waiting. Make sure to bring your necessary documents too! Staff there were amazing and friendly :)

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
I would like to express my deep dissatisfaction with the service I received during my recent medical check-out for my Taiwan visa.
First of all, the medical check-out was not cheap — it cost me around RM400. With such a price tag, one would reasonably expect efficiency, professionalism, and proper follow-through. Unfortunately, what I experienced was the opposite.
Despite assurances from your nurse that my medical report would be updated on your app, nothing was ever uploaded. I tried emailing and following up multiple times, but the process was painfully slow, with no resolution in sight. On top of that, your doctor’s handling of foreign visa procedures was far from professional — unclear instructions on filling out forms, and making me return multiple times just to collect my report due to inexperience.
To make matters worse, at your Bangsar South branch, I was given a number to WhatsApp for assistance. I did exactly that, but no one ever returned my messages or calls. If this is meant to be a communication channel, it clearly isn’t working.
And then there is your app. I was told it was for convenience and accessibility, but since my medical report was never linked or updated, I can’t help but wonder: was the app really created for clients, or is it simply a clever way to collect our personal data and build your database?
For RM400 plus  I expected transparency, efficiency, and competent service. Instead, I was left frustrated and inconvenienced. I sincerely hope you take this complaint seriously and review your processes so that future clients do not face the same issues.

Lifecare should look into queuing system seriously to solve the issue.

While the examination process itself was tolerable, the overall experience was severely undermined by the unprofessional conduct of the front desk staff. I would strongly advise prospective clients to seek a more professional and responsive alternative.

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
This has been a ridiculous and frustrating experience as a consumer and patient.
I had my body check in October 2023 with the RM1,400++ female package. The problems started immediately: my name was not even on the appointment list despite booking one of the earliest slots. Annoying, but I thought it was just a small issue.
The major problem was with the Fibroscan test — a non-invasive ultrasound test to measure liver stiffness and fat content. The practitioner struggled to get a proper reading and had to try multiple times, saying it was difficult to “knock” the right spot between the ribs. In the end, she managed to record a result — but unfortunately, it came out abnormal, implying I had potential liver hardening issues.
Thankfully, the package included a doctor consultation. The doctor reviewed all my results, including the blood tests, and concluded that I did not seem to have liver issues. He told me to ignore the Fibroscan result. At that point, I thought the matter was closed.
However, in May 2024, when I wanted to upgrade my insurance, the abnormal Fibroscan result became a major obstacle. Despite explaining what the doctor had said, the insurance agency refused and insisted that I redo the Fibroscan and get a doctor’s verification to prove my liver was fine.
I contacted Lifecare again, thinking they would take responsibility since the original test was unreliable. My expectation was simple: redo the Fibroscan properly, have a doctor sign it off, and fix the report. Instead, Lifecare told me to redo the test at my own cost first (RM700+), and only “maybe” get a refund later after management review. To make things worse, the customer service agent implied it was partly my fault for not asking the practitioner or doctor to redo the test on the spot back in October 2023. She even “advised” me not to reveal other medical reports in the future — unprofessional and shocking to hear.
In the end, I had to spend extra — another RM700+ for a second Fibroscan, plus additional costs for getting a doctor from another hospital to verify the result, since Lifecare’s doctor couldn’t simply sign off. Eventually, my insurance was upgraded, but only after unnecessary stress and expense.
After this, I filed a complaint. Four days later, the Operations Manager called me back and said Lifecare would compensate me with a blood and urine test package. But the package was set to expire in 2024 — which made no sense, because I had just done a full check in October 2023 and wouldn’t need another until two years later. I requested to extend the validity. After some persuasion, she finally confirmed (verbally, after checking with management) that the package could be delayed until 2025.
Fast forward to September 2025: I contacted the same Operations Manager again to schedule my body check for October 2025. It turned out she had left the company a year ago. I emailed Lifecare with all the evidence (including past emails and screenshots of our WhatsApp conversation). Their reply was unbelievable — they claimed I needed to provide further proof because the agreement was only made over a phone call, but they hadn’t sent me any written confirmation. They said they could only extend the validity until September 2025.
I wrote back, pointing out that this was a compensation package for their mistake, and that I had clearly stated in emails that October was the only time I could return to KL. Why should the compensation suddenly expire in September? After further back-and-forth, they finally agreed to honor October 2025.
My conclusion:
I will never go to Lifecare again. Their professionalism and accuracy are highly questionable. Imagine if I had a serious condition that was missed because of their unreliable tests — the consequences could have been far worse. Their way of handling complaints is equally unprofessional: verbal promises with no written confirmation, later denial, pushing responsibility onto the patient, and dragging things out until the customer gives up.

Review:
UNPROFESSIONAL, INSULTING, DISCRIMINATING!
Communication from the nurse station, doctor, and person managing what's app  comms are not organize and very poorly managed. I had to proactively manage the communication because no one seems to care.
Today, I came in at 9am for a 9:30am doctor's appointment. Went straight to the 4th floor nurse station 2, told me to sit down and wait without asking for my information. Past 9:30am I wasn't called in yet, noticed the doctor was in the room, so I went straight to the room. Doctor said she hasn't received my papers. I Went to the reception, waited for 10-15 mins mins (thinking he reason is b'coz I skipped this)...taking a long time so I decided to go back to nurse station 2. I told the nurse, doctor said she has not received my papers, nurse said doctor never informed them.  That was the only time they asked for my information.
I am very upset with this experience, very unprofessional and disorganized. Nurse didn't even apologise.
7 days before this, I went to the same clinic for a procedure only to be told that the doctor cancelled the appointment without giving me a heads up. Seriously??? You only inform the patient on the day of the surgery???? I don't accept the last minute reason, and being told that it's cancelled because my insurance claim has been denied is very discriminating and insulting when I already informed the person managing the Whats App messages that I will pay myself. You all assumed I cannot pay my own bills???!!! Very unprofessional and very disrespectful. Wasted 1 day of  my leave.  Will never go back in this clinic.
The anesthesiologist guy doctor was very nice. Very concerned on my condition and always check if I was OK. Thank you!

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
Was doing my VISA application TB testing for the UK. Got there at 9:45am, came out at 1:50pm. I cannot believe how long I waited and how lost I was. People just kept telling me to wait and I sat there not knowing what’s going on. They then confused me for another woman and assumed I had already done my x-ray when I FINALLY got to see a doctor. I thought I was delirious for a second as how could I not remember myself getting the x-ray?! Then had to do the x-ray and then waited some more uncertainly. The doctor then ran past me while I was sitting on the couch saying that “your lungs are good!” (Pretty comedic actually) and then finally got called to take my… idk is it a certificate but they handed me back the piece of paper that was partly filled by me in the morning.
I don’t even know how or what to use it for?? When asking for clarification- the person also seemed to not know what’s going on 😭. Anyways, thank you for reading my rant and I sincerely hope other people do not have the same experience.
Note: appointments you make online do not matter- I booked mine for 10:15 and still waited nearly 4 hours :)
But one thing: their toilets are clean and spacious 👍

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
Extremely disappointing experience. I went in for a check-up and 2 different nurses tried to draw my blood at two different spots, but both failed. The manager, Elizabeth Lim, then stepped in and still couldn’t locate a vein even after several minutes.
I was then asked to lie down so she could “slowly find a vein,” which I refused. I have never had to lie down for a blood test in my life. After that, they called the head nurse, who tried yet another spot on my arm,  failed again.
That made 3 failed attempts. At that point I complained, only they send a doctor over. The doctor asked me to rest first. By then, almost one full hour had been wasted just trying to draw blood with no success. And yes, it was painful.
I eventually gave up and left without completing the check-up. Honestly, this was a very frustrating and uncomfortable experience. Definitely not recommended — there are many other medical centres that can do much better.

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
Absolutely terrible experience.
My parents recently did a health screening here and it was nothing short of a nightmare. We made it clear from the start that we were flying out soon and urgently needed the report on the same day, that’s the only reason we chose this pricy health screening centre.
Despite that, everything took forever. We were told to wait 4 hours for the report, so we went to a nearby mall to kill time. After 3 hours, we called to check in, instead of giving us a proper update, the guy on the phone tried to upsell my sister a health screening before even answering our question. Completely unprofessional.
Eventually, we returned and suddenly they said the report was ready. Took the prescribed medication home, the next morning, my parent felt extremely unwell. We rushed back, only to be told that the antibiotic wasn’t suitable. And guess what? We had to pay another RM190 just to get it changed.
End of story. If you’re considering this medical center, good luck, you’ll need it.

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review: This is my very first time having my health screened over here. The experience was horrendous ! I chose the earliest slot which is 745am, there were also walk in clients but they finished their test before me and I totally understand everyone has diff package and tests to go through. The best part, after I done few tests, I have been told to drink water to make my bladder full to have better ultrasound screening. There’s few ultrasound room but only 2 professional were on duty that day. I have been seeing ppl who came later than me went in and done their ultrasound, left me hanging looking at the tv waiting for them to call my number. I went to the counter back and forth to check when is my turn. I told them my bladder was going to burst and they asked me to wait. Patiently waited for 30min, it wasn’t moving at all! In the end I can’t hold anymore I went to the toilet and I started to gulp water again in case it’s my turn. So while waiting, I asked them to slot me in to which test that was available at that period. The management was bad! Sigh, after I gulped few cups of water, my bladder full until cannot take it again! I have not eaten anything, I was feeling cold, my bladder was full, from 745am till 1205pm I only completed not even 2/3 of my tests. If I didn’t keep on asking when is my turn I don’t think i can ever get my ultrasound done! I didn’t get to completed all of my tests. By the time I can go home was about 430pm. Bad experience! Really bad

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
I had an incredibly frustrating and disappointing experience at Lifecare Bangsar during my recent medical checkup. Initially, I requested an appointment for 11 a.m., but I was told this time was “too late” and was forced to book for 10 a.m. Despite arriving on time, I waited nearly an hour just to register due to an apparent shortage of staff and inefficient processes. Ironically, my registration was only completed at 11:10 a.m., which completely negates the earlier insistence on avoiding an 11 a.m. appointment.
The delays didn’t end there. The wait for the doctor’s consultation felt endless. At one point, the receptionist called me, and I assumed it was finally my turn, only to be told to wait downstairs instead. When I was finally seen, the doctor asked a few basic questions and quickly concluded the session. To my disappointment, I wasn’t provided with any physical reports and was directed to access them via their app.
The app, however, was an absolute nightmare to use. I was unable to access my report, so I contacted their support team. Despite being reassured multiple times that they would get back to me, no one ever followed up. I had to call again the following day, only to receive the same dismissive response. The person on the phone seemed unable to comprehend my issue, which was both frustrating and unprofessional. It’s now January 17th, and my medical checkup was on January 4th. More than two weeks have passed, and I am still dealing with the same unresolved issue.
To make matters worse, their WhatsApp “support” is nothing more than an unhelpful chatbot that doesn’t address concerns effectively. For a medical center with such a strong reputation, this level of disorganization and lack of customer care is deeply disappointing. I felt disrespected, ignored, and let down throughout the entire process. I will never revisit Lifecare Bangsar, and I cannot recommend it to others.

Review:

There is a numbering system (unlike several other medical centres where we felt lost, confused and causes long waiting time and miscommunication) and proper heads-up on waiting time. Even waiting for half hour, the nurses notified so that we can either wait or go have a coffee/ meal first.
Customer service team are excellent, guiding us on where to go, what to do etc especially for first timers at the medical center is very appreciated.
Nurses/ medical personnel performing the tests are very gentle and courteous. Reassuring when we are nervous.
Doctor is very patient in explaining results and options.
Pharmacy and cashier counter personnel are efficient.
All staff are consistent in their excellent service. It's evident there are proper training in place.
Thank you for the pleasant experience.

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
I think the first touchpoint with potential clients are always the most important - and that either brings you sales, or not.
At the Starling mall roadshow today, we were met by a few very welcoming and friendly staff from LifeCare who invited us to do a quick and “free” health and heart check. However, after being seated down for further explanation, the woman who attended to us was very unprofessional.
First, we were required to fill in some sort of “LifeCare loyalty form” which the woman refused to further explain what our data would be used for - though I believe a quick health check would not require us to submit such personal details at all. Basically, no transparency to why we need to give our details away, and the purpose of it.
Secondly, the woman was very unprofessional with her explanation throughout. After explaining “very” briefly what our BMI check results meant, she just threw us a few ongoing promotions without any explanation. We had to guess what the suitable package for us was and when asked, she obviously could not tell us what was so special about their packages that make their “RM688” promo so attractive. Fortunately her service was bad enough that we didn’t want to sign up because comparison with other hospitals proved theirs much more expensive.
Thirdly, the front of house staff initially promoted their “free” heart check. However, when checked with the woman who attended to us, she declined such service to us. Quoting her, “it’s free, but you come back later lah after your dinner”. We wanted to do instantly, why did we have to wait? LOL.
That completely diminished the good perception we had towards LifeCare. Such unprofessional staff only reflects the same on the company.

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review: Very surprised at the difference in experiences today versus my first time in 2022. Showed up at 8am previously and completed my final consultation by 5pm -- I did think it was long and didn't expect half a day, but it was a comprehensive health check-up from blood, urine, ultrasound image tests, stress and ECG all the way to consultation. Today, I came in at 8.50am, waited till 10 for registration, did urine and blood within 30 minutes and completed height and weight shortly after before 11am. Have been waiting since (now 3.30pm) for my stress test (and I'm sure this isn't part of the test). The whole experience where staff would guide you and not have you wait more than 30 minutes for a section was a lot more seamless in 2022, but today was ridiculous. It really seems that they've just decided to overbook themselves with customers and neglect how long people have to wait. If I were to guess, it's poor upper management and in no way reflective of the good work most of the staff are doing -- the simplest thing to implement here is just to give people better estimations of waiting times instead of "wait until we call you". Very poor experience.

Do better for your patients that you are serving and not just profit from them and give them a terrible system and call it a day.

Would not recommend to anyone who values their time.
Hope Lifecare improves their system so that we dont wait endlessly for a checkup

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
We have been coming for the Lifecare Gold Package for four consecutive years now. The staff have always been friendly and supportive, which we truly appreciate. However, the waiting time remains a concern.
In previous years, we usually came around 8.30am — our checkup typically finished around 1–2 p.m., and by the time we completed the doctor and dietitian consultations, it was already 4–5 p.m.
This year, we decided to come early at 7:45 a.m and we are lucky that it wasn’t very crowded today. The checkup itself went smoothly, and we finished by 11:30 a.m. However, after lunch, we had to wait until 2:45 p.m. before being informed that the imaging results were just ready — and that the queue to see the doctor was now very long. The staff then asked if we would prefer to schedule another day for the doctor’s consultation, even though we had already waited more than three hours and had taken leave for the day.
We hope that the management will look into this issue and find ways to improve the process, especially regarding result readiness and scheduling, so that patients’ time can be better managed.

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
Made an appointment for mammogram package in advance and was informed that it’ll be a maximum of 3 hours.
Upon arrival, I was told that “there are many people ahead of you today so would you like to come back another day?”. Now, why would your clinic accept appointments for specific timings if you can’t manage your system??
As I don’t live so near the clinic, I said it’s ok as we already made the appointment and drove all the way there. We were assured it won’t take more than 3 hours to complete an ultrasound, mammogram, bone density check and consultation.
While the clinic was packed, it started out well as I was seen promptly for mammogram. Then it all went downhill! My mom and I were back to back in queue and while I was having my mammogram, I saw that her name and number was next in line for the scan. However, after 30 mins, she was still waiting there and we realised that there were 2 people that were slotted in front of her! After checking with the counter again, she was told to sit for “observation” first and have lunch as our next test was going to be over 45 minutes wait.
So here’s the kicker. If you aren’t a “VIP” or someone with a “title”, then be prepared to wait as they’ll cut the queue with their personal concierge! A lot of them around walking in and out without having to wait hours on end while the “commoners” are treated without any respect for their time.
My BMI (InBody) test was taken immediately AFTER my lunch, which of course, isn’t going to be an accurate reading. The dietitian and nutrition consult was a waste of time as well as all she did was read from the paper and insisting I do hardcore workouts, disregarding the age and any medical conditions. It felt more like one of those slimming Center scams at one point.
To cut the story short, we waited for over 6 hours in the clinic just for a simple procedure and my mom’s medical report and doctors consultation wasn’t even done! It was always “please wait, there are 1-2 more pax in front of you”.
It was truly a horrendous experience and waste of time. My mom managed to get refunded without a medical report as it wasn’t worth waiting much longer! Even half the staff had left by then and people who came in after her had all been seen.
If you all plan to go there,  perhaps register as some Datuk and you’ll get preferential treatment and a different experience.

1. The registration has 5 counters open but took 1 hour to register 10 person. It was 12.28pm when i done register.
2. Submitted my health screening form to counter 2 and they lost my paper. Only when i realise few people who came later than me already got their blood test done, i went to check with counter, and they franticly search for my paper and they say they couldnt find it. The male employee was nice enough to immediately handle this but it has wasted 45 mins. It was 1.12pm when my blood sample is drawn.
3. After all tests are done at 1.45pm, nursing counter told me to come back at 3pm for my report, when i ask for the report at 3pm they say no, it is 4.15pm.
4. Also, when test are done at 1.45pm i saw there were still a few tests highlighted in green that i havent done, when i check with the staff, they say, all tests are done, the green ones are optional. But when i check for report status at 3pm, the staff pointed at one of the green highlighted test and asked me, "so for this audiometry test, are you not doing it?" I was baffled with the question as i checked with them earlier and they confirmed I've completed all. So, somehow i "gave up" a necessary test that required to complete my check up.
5. I went again at 4.25pm to check on it, the nurse told me "maybe another 15 minutes some more, you wait la"
6. I ask to have the report send to my email, the nurse say "can, you can leave now". Why is e-report option not presented until i ask for it. I could have left at 1.45pm but 2.5 hours was wasted and i left without a report at 4.30pm
It was a very smooth process when i came on 2022 for health screening that's why i pick here again, but today i spent total 5 hours in this medical centre, and 4 hours of out it, is just for waiting.

Review: Went for health screening on a Saturday, was told that their lab had issues and wouldn’t be able to produce the blood test report on the same day. I came back on a Friday, made an online appointment for doctor’s consultation at 12.15pm, I reached the place at 12.05pm was told by the reception that I need to wait for 30 to 45 mins but after two hours I’m still waiting to see the doctor while typing this review here. The coordination is terrible. If I knew the wait is going to be this long, I would have opted for a phone consultation. 2 hours of wait just to meet the doctor and receive the medical checkup report even after making an appointment is ridiculous, completely unacceptable. I took time off from work not expecting this long wait and I ended up rescheduling a few work calls just because of this.

Review: Went there this week for a visa healthcheck up. For the registration, the queue time is 15-30 minutes long despite having 3 counters open and just one queue number in front of me, there was no one else waiting. The blood taking and chest x ray did not take a long time, however when i needed to have a consultation for the dr for visa purposes, the waiting time was 2 hours. It is absolutely nonsense. The only reason why i went to this clinic was because it is recognised by Australia and my agent recommended it. If you have other options, please do not come here. I came for another visit to ask the Dr to fill a form for the visa vaccination records, and i had to wait for 2 hours. If you have the time to wait, feel free to visit this clinic. (Fyi, the clinic is so big and empty but the service and waiting time is so long. )

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
I arrived at 12:20 p.m. 14/10/2024
to receive my medical check up report and was informed that there were few patients ahead of me. However, by 2:20 p.m., I noticed that several patients who arrived after me were being seen first. I did bring it up when I vividly remembered one patient after me was called.When I asked a lady staff member—who was wearing a sleeveless black top and had fake eyelashes—I was told they just wanted to say hi to the doctor.I mean it was such a long wait😭,despite not so many patients were there,you made me wait 2 hour plus.I remember she went inside the room to inform the dr something too while I was about to enter and showed annoyance while communicating with others.But how much patience you want me to be-first it was the long wait and then this🥹.At 3p.m only the doctor managed to see me and within 15 minutes done.
I’m concerned about the fairness of the process while others seemed to receive priority based on personal interactions with Jas ong and another promoter raises questions about the purpose of the numbering system.I also encountered a similar situation during my ultrasound appointment. I would really appreciate it if there could be more consistency and professionalism to ensure all patients are treated equally and fairly.
There are many great staff members at the clinic too-the person who drew my blood, the doctor who performed my echo along with the nurse assisting him, the staff who administered my Hepatitis A injection, Dr who did my fibroscan and the one who handled my registration. However, the positive experiences with these individuals are overshadowed by the unprofessionalism of a few others. I sincerely hope to see improvements soon, as it’s unfortunate that the kindness and professionalism of these excellent staff members are being dimmed by the actions of a few.

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
We regret coming here. 10 years ago their customer service was not this bad. We're here for our TB Test for a UK Visa. However their customer service did not reflect the amount of money they charged us! Their customer service is simply so bad! Their centre is actually the most expensive in Peninsular Malaysia for a UK Visa TB Test but their service is worst than your typical government hospital. Mind u this is in Bangsar!
At this Lifecare Centre nobody smiles at u, no one greets u, no "good afternoon" not even a "thank u" will be said to u. Even government hospitals are friendlier than this.
When I arrived, the man at the counter on Level G was already projecting his attitude! His attitude was as if we were disturbing him! Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
If you are planning to take the TB test and medical check-up for your UK visa application, read this.
The TB test - the concierge guy told us not to include any bin/binti in the TB form, even when the passport and CAS form has bin/binti. Such indiscrepancy could be a ground for a costly Visa rejection. Our agent asked us to ensure the name in the TB report tally with the CAS and passport, but the centre is currently saying that is not their practice to include bin/binti. Other medical centres have no problem with us including bin/binti.
The other thing is the medical report won't be ready on the same day, unlike other TB centres. You'd have to wait for them to text you to collect. You can only colllect the TB report on the same day.
I dont know how they got all these ppl to take a photo and write nice reviews with their concierge people on it. That is very unusual, especially when the service we got was a far cry than what was written... hmmm... The concierge was the worst person we've encountered, and I got the same feedback from other people who went there within a few days from me. No greetings, no smile, just arrogant. And everyone I know who went there complained the same thing. Go figure.
My advice is think twice before coming here. Be safe, go to other centres.

Would highly suggest to go elsewhere for health checkups.

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
Came here for my corporate health checkup on Saturday morning.
Overall service is great & efficient. However, The arrangement of going for the different assessment is good but could have been better.
I was disappointed with how lifecare deal with one of my test as I have initially asked for exchange as I was not suitable for the test ( as it was part of the package) & I paid for it ( no choice).  They insisted that I can't exchange it & can only defer it to someone else & even gave only 2 weeks duration... money wasted down the drain.... hopefully lifecare is more emphatic towards customers & listened to us more....
Some tips below
1) for those who have gastric issues like me,  take plenty of water after urine test so that you can queue for the ultrasound of pelvis & abdomen as this still requires empty stomach.
2) Go for your light refreshments after you have done the blood test & ultrasound so that your waiting time for the rest of tests is more bearable
3) Go for all the tests done on first floor so that you don't need to keep going up & down as ENT is on the 4th floor
4) there are 4 options for light refreshments
Done all the tests & doctor consultation by 12pm 👌
Edit : came here again for health checkup in May 2025. Service is still good,  however,  the breakfast option is so so given they have more outsource it to a cafe at ground floor. I finish all the test by 9am, was told that the report is only ready past 11am plus doctor consultation which I find it a bit long to hang around just for that.  I collected the report on another day instead.

Review:

The next morning I called to ask for the results again and was given empty promises. It is now 26h later and still no email and now they’re closed until Monday. Also your call would keep getting hung up instead of being answered, and the WhatsApp Chat is virtually useless.
This is on top of the whole centre being insanely slow. Waited 1.5h just to even register as a patient (already booked appointment online prior), and the whole day took 6h just for 1 blood test, 1 chest X ray and 1 doctor’s consultation (which they make you do just to order the blood tests)…
And if you’d notice, all the replies to comments are the standard same generic copy-paste response with no actual effort to look into the matter and resolve it so they can improve.

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
The appointment system at this medical checkup centre was extremely unsatisfactory. Despite having an appointment at 8:15 AM, I was not registered until 09:34 AM, rendering the purpose of having an appointment system futile.
To compound matters, the checkup itself was quite disorganized and it took me a laborious 7 hours to complete. I was left clueless as to when my next checkup was scheduled and had to repeatedly approach the nurse counter for information.
Furthermore, even after completing all the tests, it was already 2:30 PM, and I had to inquire about the availability of my report rather than receiving an update proactively. The staff were unable to provide me with an estimated waiting time and simply asked me to sit and wait, which was quite frustrating.
As someone who has visited several different medical checkup centres every year, I can confidently say that this was by far the worst experience I have ever had.

I told them I had my meals at the lounge and ready to go for the ultrasound; the staff told me I have to wait another 2 hours at least for my turn..so what is the point of having an appointment??? Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
I had a really bad throat infection and was there to meet the ENT specialist.
What a horrible experience it was. Dr Shantini was absolutely rude and unkind. I was in great pain, throat was completely blocked and couldn’t talk, I had everything written down on a note yet she insisted for me to verbalise my condition. Even asked what my nationality, which I thought was VERY unnecessary.
I waited 1.5 hours before I could see her, and when I finally saw her, it was less than 5 mins and she referred me to another hospital, because she couldn’t treat my condition. She charged my insurance RM300, which I felt like was a rip off, considering the encounter I had.
Do not recommend here if you are looking for an ENT specialist.

Review:
Despite all of the comments view here.  I still went for my medical check-up there.  Was doing the Gold + type.  Arrived there at 7.45am as requested and finished at 5.30pm.  Too long wait.  By the time I finished, was exhausted, then the doctor didn't really do good explanation to me but rather doing just like others said, doing hard-sell.  Furthermore, didn't have chance to do the nutritionist part as it was already 5.30pm and they punched off at 5.00pm.  When I got the report, no one bother to ask me about the nutritionist advice part but as I was totally exhausted and hungry (imagine since fasting the night before and having only very tiny portion of refreshment in the middle).
Agreed with one of the reviewers here saying after the check-up, I am more lost in my health condition as there isn't any precise explanation from the doctor.  The doctor seems more interested to sell you medication than explaining with patience in the result of the check-up results. Called up the next day wanting to talk to someone about the vague explanation to get some assurance but saying will call back but waited for the whole day and no call.  Hope they will call one day.
Though some of the staff during check-up were friendly and helpful but the one checking the bones was rude.
Besides all of the above.  This centre is very clean, comfortable and good facility.  If only they will improve a bit the doctors side by giving more interest and attention in explaining the results conditions, that will be perfect.

Review:
I first knew about LifeCare Medical Centre a couple of years ago but never had the opportunity to visit the place. Had to visit this time round for a medical test with the family and I was not disappointed. I was attended to by Ms Jess Ong before my visit; she was professional and had deep knowledge about the medical centre's products and services (was also given an analysis on the different options that are available - truly professional indeed).
I was also pleased with the service levels (in terms of speed and attentiveness, which are important factors for a medical centre - at least for me) that I experienced during the visit. The nurses were very polite and also patient towards my family's requests.
Will certainly be back if I require any other medical procedures in the future (hopefully, it wont be so soon!!).

Just some constructive feedback.

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
Had a not so good experience whilst I was doing my checkup here. Was requested to do my X-ray twice because during the first one, the staff did not instruct properly, thus somewhat of a sloppy outcome for the first x-ray. Thus, needing a second one afterward. The thing is, none of them contacted me during my waiting period to tell me my first one was not successful and required a second one, until I walked up to ask if my report was ready for collection.
The worst thing was, whilst waiting for the report, before being able to see my results and consult with the doctor, a lady working at the counter ‘in a black blazer coat’ came to tell me :’ it’s better to check twice, at least not when things are spotted, we can treat it early.’
I looked at her in disbelief and was taken aback.
I replied:’ did you find something in my first x-ray scan, that’s why you asked for a second? Did you all actually find something!??’ My heart dropped.
She replied:’ Oh no no, we don’t know yet. But it’s best to discuss with your doctor on further treatments and further testing etc.’
She added on:’ of course it could be nothing to worry, let’s see.’
I was left speechless. I literally sat there in utter shock and disappointment that as people working in the medical/care industry could be so careless in the way you relay news to patients. The thing is, you’re not a licensed physician and have no medical qualifications to explain to me on my results, let alone none of you had laid eyes on my results yet at that juncture.
Why in the world would you say the things the way you said it, when no results were out at that point?
Was your intention to sell more tests and treatments? Or were you genuinely caring for your patients that might receive not so good news?
I’m leaving this review so that Lifecare’s upper management could enlighten on the Do’s and Don’ts when it comes to what to and what not to tell patients, before consulting with the doctor.
‘We saw something’
‘Discuss further treatments’
ARE NOT THE WORDS TO SAY TO A PATIENT, BEFORE ANY RESULTS OR DOCTOR CONSULTATION HAD BEEN CONDUCTED.
However, I would still love to give credit to Doctor Alex for being so cheerful and patient with explaining the results, as well as bringing ease to the situation, after the hell I’ve been through in the waiting area. Thank God, scans were clear.
Lifecare, do better to teach your radiology technicians as well as those wear black blazers around the counters. They should refrain from commenting further when it comes to situations like these, until a doctor has been consulted.

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
The specialist requested to move the appointment earlier but was late by almost 40 minutes. He even arrived 10 mins later than the original appointment time. The consultation on the health check up was very brief; the specialist was basically saying that the report was all ok. The total consultation time was about 30 mins. It was almost entirely (about 20 mins) based on a condition that I mentioned to the specialist (urologist) during the medical history check that wasn’t even in the check up that I signed up for and also not within the specialty of the specialist (it was a gastrointestinal issue). The consultation about my gastrointestinal issue was also very basic, the specialist was just telling me about the possible cause of the issue and told me to get help. There was no examination or any recommendation given because there wasn’t any checking that has been done anyway. There were no consultation at all, ie: the specialist didn’t mention a single word about the additional package that I signed up for, including urea breath test, thyroid hormone test, vitamin D test and CIMT.
I reflected the issue to the customer care manager, but the only resolution provided by her was that the management will have a discussion with the doctor.
The only good thing about my entire experience was the helpful nurse.

Review: A very disorganised health testing centre. They couldn’t handle the capacity of people wanting to test on the same day. Classic example of corporate greed as they continued to allow people to test at their facility even though it was over their limit. We were told to come back 2 weeks for mere consultation and they could not even slot myself and my girlfriend in for a quick consultation the very next day. The staff at the imaging counter had the audacity to tell us to come back another day to test as there were too many people. Pretty ridiculous as she is basically asking us to fast all over again just to go through the same nightmare. If you are a person working in an office, I suggest you look elsewhere to get your testing done as you’ll have to allocate 2 days of your annual leave in anticipation of the messy management. Probably better to just do your health checks at your regular clinic with the same facilities since you probably wont get your results the same day. Will never come back here to test again

Review: I went there to do a x-ray, the place is quite nice, the staff is also generally polite, of course the price is also higher than other places. However, i was not happy with the waiting time, given that so little patients there and so many staff, I expect to complete the whole process within 1 hour (this was what my experience in other places). However, i have waited quite some time for the x-ray, then even longer time for report, total time spent is about 2 to 3 hours. Also, it seems like there is no one central system to control the process flow, staff is doing a lot of calling, finding to get things done. Another issue is that, if they expect us to wait for so long, should there actually tell us to set our expectation right? My experience is staff there just ask you to wait here or there, without telling you the expected waiting time, no number, if you not asking around, you probably will be blindly waiting, not sure what happen. In short, the process is really bad, slow and customer friendly.

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
🔔Unprofessional Sales Tactics at Health Screening Centre.
During my first visit to LifeCare Medical Centre Bangsar with my partner for a test, but our experience was marred by unprofessional behavior from an Indian saleswoman (Mrs.Jeya)
Moreover, before she offered the 11K treatment, my partner underwent a 3K cancer blood test as indicated in the pamphlet shown by the her. However, we were shocked when she proceeded to offer us the 11K treatment afterward, which was completely unexpected and unwelcome!
Despite clearly expressing my financial limitations and declining an expensive treatment, the Indian saleswoman persisted and even went as far as contacting me more than 5 times early in the morning  while we were still sleeping!

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
I was there last week Wednesday to do my annual ultrasound of abdomen, pelvis and thyroid and mammogram and ultrasound of breast. Used to do it in Pantai Hospital but decided to try Lifecare. Arrived at 10 am and did not finish until 3 pm..The wait was extremely long n tiring n exhausting
I had a very stressful and emotionally draining experience. After waiting for almost 2 hrs, I finished all the scanning but was suddenly asked to go in to redo the breast ultrasound again as  the radiologist saw sthg in my mammogram. The 2nd ultrasound conducted by the sonographer  seemed clear n the  consultant radiologist came to check n confirmed it clear n told  me the mammogram may not have  been  properly compressed .. I was then  told the report  would take another 45 mins to 1 hr to be ready and then  another wait to see the dr for consultation. So I went for lunch thinking by the time I come back I would be able to see the dr. But unfortunately after lunch I was told to do another round of mammogram again and this time it was an extremely painful process  as  the technician fully compressed my breast to the maximum until I was screaming in pain. . After the second mammogram I asked the technician why and if everything was ok.. All she said was wait for Dr to tell you. I was then told to wait outside and waited for another 1 hr.. Imagine the stress I have to go through during that 1 hr of waiting not knowing why I have to do 2 ultrasound and 2 mammogram. I do appreciate that they are being careful but I dont appreciate being kept in the dark especially since it was an error in the first mammogram.. I have to ask my husband to go home as the wait was getting too long and the mental torture I went through during that long 1 hour wait was horrendous . By the time  I saw the  Dr, I was exhausted..The good news was everything was fine.
I was in tears by the time I finished 5 hrs later at 3 pm.. Exhausted from stress.. So it was an unpleasant experience..

The receptionist also failed to inform us the suitable tests to do despite knowing our health condition and later on when we asked further, they tried suggesting additional tests out of the package they told us to sign up for. In addition, they claim to serve light refreshment as part of the medical packages but the mini cafeteria isn’t up and ready to serve breakfast in the morning. Overall the experience wasn’t pleasant in my opinion. This probably won’t be in our list the next time we do full medical checkup.

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
I'm here for a health check for my Australian student visa application (subclass 500). Overall, I'm satisfied with their streamlined checking procedures. The staffs are very friendly too.
I'm here from 8.15 to 9.55am on a Saturday, the whole process was about 1.5 hours if you reach here earlier. It cost me RM285, it was a 18% raise in price as compared to 2015 (I did my visa health check here as well). This price includes chest x-ray, physical check, urine test.
Do print the electronic form from their webpage, and fill part A and B before you come.
The White Dental on the second floor is my go-to-place too, Dr Sia Nin is very good.

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
It is my first time getting a comprehensive full body checkup and I would definitely recommend others to come here. Everything is quite systematic though there are still much room for improvement from the staff/ centre.
Some doctors can look quite intimidating and unfriendly due to the lack of smile but they are actually quite nice and answered all my questions in detail. It is understandable as I've worked in retail industry before and it can be tiring to keep smiling all the time everyday. I got there at 8am and finished everything at 3pm (inclusive of an hour+ break which I left for food and shower)
A few suggestions for/ during the checkup:
1. A shirt and a robe will be provided for changing. I find the shirt being very redundant as you still got to take it off during some checks so luckily I wore the robe only. Lockers will be provided as well.
2. For abdomen ultrasound, remember to drink plenty of water in the morning or an hour prior the checkup, your bladder needs to be full for the check. Else the doctor will ask you to go for other stations in your checklist and come back again when you feel like peeing, which you will then have to wait again.
3. Once your blood sample and body weight analysis are taken, you can break fast and have the complimentary light refreshments at a small cafeteria in the corner. This helps to energize yourself for other tests. I wasn't told and only managed to eat once I have completed about 80% of my tests. It would be nice if I was told that I could at least eat something halfway through so the waiting could be more bearable.
4. Remember to eat something light to prep yourself for the stress test (if applicable) as it requires fast walk and running in order to complete the test. This can be quite intense for people who do not workout much. Make sure to bring or wear sport shoes and tie your shoelaces tight (Mine came off halfway but the test cannot be paused else the test will need to restart again)
4. Once you have completed all the tests stationed on the First Floor, you can change into your own clothings. As for ENT and Eye Assessment, it will be on other floors. I was not informed that I can change. It can be very uncomfortable or insecure for females to take lifts/ walk around in public without our upper inner wears. Luckily I changed for my own sake.
5. The longest wait (at least 30 mins or more) I had was for the eye assessment. It is located at G floor and it's an outsourced eye specialist so the patients there are not just from Lifecare. Would suggest to go for this test slightly earlier to prevent the crowd and waiting time.
6. If you are really very hungry that you need a proper meal, you can leave the centre for a meal nearby once you have completed all your tests. Come back again in an hour or so to collect your reports for doctor consultation and dietary nutrition care assessment.
7. During doctor's consultation, if there is any test required for a specific check for certain concerns based on your report, can try to add on/ top up on the same day to be entitled to some promo if applicable.

Reviewer's name: Mohd Syameer Firdaus Bin Mohd Shafiaai
Review:
This is my second visit for Aussie visa purpose to LifeCare. The overall experience has not changed over the years: they are both systematic and straight forward.
The medical staffs i.e. doctor, phlebotomist, radiographer and the nurses were courteous and quick at what they are doing. The staff at the registration counter is good as well. My only concern is that the officer at the payment counter is quite rude and this is very uncalled for given that it is where payment is made and she should have at least be more courteous and respectful to the person who is paying. Utterly disappointed by such a rough housing by the payment counter in a private healthcare setting.
Hopefully LifeCare can look into this matter and do the needful. Nevertheless, thumbs up to the systematic process and professional medical staffs.

Review: My mom has been going here for her cancer treatment since November 2021. We love the service of the staff at Onco Life Centre. However, from what we have observed, this place has no concierge and it is not an OKU-friendly place (apart from the ramp that they have provided). From my observation, there are a lot of patients who come with wheelchairs; the relatives could not drop them off at the lobby as there are only security guards (two of them were kind enough to help around but recently they were stationed far away from the lobby drop off point). As a result, most of the patients and relatives have to park at the basement, and enter the building using the basement entrance. Now, here is the additional problem. There is a ramp for wheelchair, but the doors are not and automated door. Therefore it is not user friendly. Me myself have experienced an OKU driver trying to enter the building alone, struggled to open the door and wheel himself in. So, we hope they can do something about this. Upgrade the facility or provide a concierge that can assist the patients, family member to send the patient upstairs to the clinic.

There is a ramp for wheelchair, but the doors are not and automated door. Therefore it is not user friendly. Me myself have experienced an OKU driver trying to enter the building alone, struggled to open the door and wheel himself in. So, we hope they can do something about this. Upgrade the facility or provide a concierge that can assist the patients, family member to send the patient upstairs to the clinic.

Nevertheless, it is now 2pm and I'm still waiting for my turn for ultrasound. I was told to keep my stomach empty for better ultrasound result. Mind you I have only been drinking water since last night, and I'm having headache caused by hunger and low sugar.
My question is, why can't they start the body check-up with ultrasound which preferably to be carried out with empty stomach before all the hearing test, eye test, etc.
This is just inconsiderate and unpleasant experience.

5 star for the Medical Center but giving you a 3 star because of her.

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review: I have many yearly check up in various places and this has got to be the worst. Firstly I must comment their staffs were excellent and helpful.   This is my first time in Lifecare and due to Covid 19 I chose this place because it’s near to my house even though it cost the same as higher end Prince Court that offer even more comprehensive test. Part of the test included is thyroid function. I was surprised when I saw my result that only tested with T4. What about T3 and TSH? I have hyperthyroidism and I know those 2 are really important indication. In all my years of doing check up, this is the only place that doesn’t include the other IMPORTANT test. When I told one of the staff, she said even their more expensive package doesn’t include this test. She said if I need it there will be additional charges. Unbelievable. Is it because thyroid medicine is cheap and not profitable? One box only cost RM12. I see during consultation your doctor emphasized so much for me to buy cholesterol medicine and hepatitis injections. All my check up in various places include this. Just showing T4 is meaningless. This will be my first and last.

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
I would like to express my anger and disappointment on your service.
On 6-Sep-2016, I brought my father-in-law (FIL), a 70-year-old, to do a full body check up by using the Package A of the RM23,000 for 10 times package that I purchased earlier.
We were told that it takes only 4 hours from beginning till we get the reports, and in between, while waiting for report, my FIL could go for breakfast.
So we arrived before 8am (registration done at 7.55am) and waited patiently for the checkup.
From my past experience, and the information given, I expected my FIL could go to eat some proper breakfast around 9.30am to 10.30am
In the beginning, everything was going smoothly, so I left my FIL at your centre and went back to my office nearby to do my work at 10am, and my brother-in-law was on the way to Life Care Centre to bring his father to breakfast.
At that time, he was waiting to do the ECG and Stress Test, which I expect would be the last session before he can eat something.
I told your sales representative, Kam, and also a nurse on duty, that please inform my FIL that he could go for breakfast.
To my surprise, after I’ve done my meeting at 1pm, I was told that my father-in-law was still waiting and not being told that he could go for some food!!!
I quickly ran to CENTRE Life Care and asked them what happened, and they some more argue with me that it’s some communication problems?!
When everything is done, we got the report and consultation from doctor, it was already 2pm, my FIL then went for lunch (without breakfast) and finally home at 4pm+.
And my FIL complained that he’s having gastric and vomiting problem now.
We didn’t get ANY compensation but some apologies.
I AM VERY VERY DISAPPOINTED WITH YOUR SERVICE AND ARRANGEMENT.
My family members and myself have no confidence to carry out the body checkup with Life Care anymore.
After much consideration, I’ve decided to ask for REFUND for the balance of my RM20,700.00.
My family is MOST IMPORTANT to me, I don’t want them to suffer and take the risk of getting any harm.

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
I reach here 8.30am n wait until 3pm just for health screening. Staff all not attendive and keep saying had to wait.Accompany my son and husband here to do blood test, ABI test, Ultrasound Pelvic +Abdomen, CT calcium score test, US Carotid IMT, Fibroscan.. My husband add on RM200 for uroflow scan at the time buy package.
Long wait until our turn for Ultrasound get done around 12pm, went to eat our complementary meal ( for those wt package only). After finish eating we go back to 1st floor for the report at 1pm and waiting our queue for doctor consultation wt the report... Wait until 1.30pm , suddenly call my husband name for Uroflow test where we don't know still have test not yet done. From 1pm-1.30pm I had go counter several times asking need how long time wait for our turn meet doctor... They answer the report haven't ready, I show the Lifecare app that ask me install from morning , report already shows in app, what to wait... They said wait relevant department print n send to front counter only can arrange to meet doctor. No one inform us have to drink more water to get 150ml urine for uroflow test., my husband fail to do the test because the urine volume not achieve unable to get reading.. Then ask my husband drink water to wait the urine full only can do the test... Already 1.45pm , I start make noise n complaint, my husband n my son very tired n angry how long have to wait for report n meet doctor where still have uroflow haven't done.. Then we choose to quit the Uroflow test and ask for refund as it is a top up option  at RM200... More angry the operation manager comes to me with a refund form of RM188 saying there is processing fees for refund. I not agree n inform I need a letter mention there is processing fees with the formula of calculation only I will sign... By 2.15pm our turn to meet doctor, the operation manager comes to the room n show me refund form for RM194... I very angry scold her loudly : I already told I pay RM200, refund also RM200... If less than RM200 show me letter mentiond the calculation... I will not sign if refund is not RM200 without any letter regarding refund calculation. Doctor more funny, asking me lots of health question before explain report, she thought I am  the one do the test... I ask doctor do u know who is the one do the test, is my husband not me.. She replied aiya I see the name end wt San I thought is lady... Thought? Doctor, the report sticker got name, IC number ( odd or even is female or male) and the gender too... How come u say thought? After explain 2 person report, once I come out from doctor consultation, operation manager bring me the refund form with RM200, I signed.. Then they chase me go back and pass the report to pharmacy counter... I wait for doctor prescription slip for my husband n son... Operation manager said u can go back now, I will WhatsApp to u later... I felt up to argue and leave... How can I buy medicine wt showing the photo in my phone to pharmacy where I don't know whether the medicine is only can buy with physical doctor prescription slip... The worst experience I had where I went many hospital for health screening. Never go a screening centre with such not professional service. Reading in report youport in the app n physical print out also got different, using different range. Such a messy screening centre... Advice not to go here for health screening. 8.30am-3pm , 1.5hr for ultrasound queue, 2 hrs for report and doctor consultation. cancel for top up option will not get refund.

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
The incredibly long waiting time was unreasonable and very disappointing. I completed all the other screenings within about 1.5 hours, and had to wait another 2.5 hours just for the ultrasound.
If ultrasound is the major bottleneck, the centre should consider having more ultrasound slots or facilities available to accommodate the number of patients. The scheduling was especially frustrating because ultrasound is generally recommended to be done on an empty stomach, yet the waiting time was so long that I almost experienced low blood sugar and felt like I might faint. I had to drinking oat milk just to prevent myself from feeling unwell.
I understand that delays can happen, but a 2.5 hour wait after completing the other screenings is excessive, especially when patients are required to fast beforehand. Better scheduling and capacity management would make the whole health screening experience much more comfortable and efficient.

Review:
I did the Diamond Screening Package. The only way to book was via their whatsapp chatbot, which told me that my booking was for 11am. Little did I know that I could have very well come earlier than that and just then get whatever number. As a result, by the time I came at 11am, there were countless of people ahead of me and I spent HOURS to get my tests done. You'd think taking the higher end of the screening package accords some prioritisation esp given  the numerous tests one had to do - do not expect this.
My last test was done only at 5pm, by which time they told me I needed to come back another day for my results and medical consult, which was infuriating.
On a positive note - the person drawing my blood did an excellent job and was highly skilled at poking with the needle.

Place: LifeCare Diagnostic Medical Centre, Bangsar South
Review:
One of the worst experiences I’ve had with a clinic.
The service was incredibly slow, and the communication was even worse. My client arrived early in the morning because we were told the medical report would be ready in about 3 hours. We planned the day based on that timeline.
After waiting the entire day, we were suddenly told the report would only be available in 3 working days. If that is the actual turnaround time, why tell patients it will be ready in 3 hours? Setting unrealistic expectations only wastes people’s time and causes unnecessary frustration.
To make matters worse, the WhatsApp customer service was almost non-existent. Messages were left unanswered for hours, and we had to keep chasing for updates. For a clinic that provides services to insurance panel clients, I expected much better coordination and responsiveness.
The entire process felt disorganised, and no one seemed to take ownership of the situation. Instead of providing updates, we were left waiting and wondering what was happening.
Patients deserve honest communication and efficient service. If you cannot meet the timeline given, at least be transparent from the beginning instead of making patients wait all day only to change the expected completion time later.
I sincerely hope the management reviews its customer service standards and operational efficiency because the current experience falls far below expectations.
